“Europe has six weeks of aviation fuel left.”

Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is important to avoid “quantity rationing” that is in Asia’s future, and also Europe if the situation continues, says Egyptian-American economist and former CEO of PIMCO, Mohamed El-Erian.

Mohamed El-Erian was speaking to Ayesha Hazarika on Times Radio Drive. Listen live every Saturday and Sunday from 4-7pm.

“I think that he is very happy to attack the Pope. But it does make some around him a little bit squeamish.”

Donald Trump remains “very happy to attack the Pope” despite unease among some of his Catholic allies, after posting an image on Truth Social appearing to depict himself as “a religious figure,” says Washington editor at The Times and The Sunday Times, Katy Balls.

Katy Balls was speaking to Rod Liddle on Times Radio. Listen live every Saturday from 10am-1pm.

author: Times News
description:
“There’s something a little bit odd going on here.”

From a football stadium twice the size of the local population to a “nowhere to nowhere” railway and EU-funded vanity projects, a visit to Viktor Orbán’s home village reveals what is a striking “physical manifestation” of corruption in Hungary, says The Times’s Europe editor Peter Conradi.

Peter Conradi was speaking to Jane Mulkerrins on Times Radio. Listen live every Saturday from 1-4pm.

description:

We bring you a special update to our groundbreaking podcast series Seventeen Years - The Andrew Malkinson Story, which first highlighted this tragic miscarriage of justice.

You can listen to the full series on The Times Investigates feed: https://pod.fo/e/3256f8

Hosts: Will Roe & Emily Dugan, Sunday Times' Special correspondent.
